dedupe_keys.name: us green space values by huc12 watershed for the wmost co benefits module

description: This dataset supplies the values needed to estimate increases in residential housing value from more green space, such as natural or forested riparian buffers and stormwater green infrastructure, for each HUC12 watershed in the United States, based on the meta-analysis of Mazotta et al. (2014), as the record cites it. It was produced by Naomi Detenbeck of the US Environmental Protection Agency as Appendix B of the Watershed Management Optimization Support Tool (WMOST) co-benefits module; the version dated 31 March 2019 is archived on Zenodo. Values are broken down by NLCD developed land-use class, for the whole watershed or distance from riparian zones (0 to 250 m and 250 to 500 m), and include housing unit density from building footprints, mean area per housing unit or building as a parcel proxy, canopy cover, population density and distance from streams. Coverage: US HUC12 watersheds. Access: one 1.2 GB zip on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: proxies such as footprint density stand in for parcel data. Simulation uses: valuing green infrastructure co-benefits in watershed and urban greening plans. Related records: PAD-US and the Vienna water features case study.
